translation_en: Ibrahim said: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us: Abd al-Samad ibn Abd al-Warith narrated to us, from Ikrimah ibn Ammar, with this hadith in its entirety. Ahmad ibn Yusuf al-Azdi al-Sulami narrated to us: al-Nadr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Ikrimah ibn Ammar, with this report.

Amr ibn Muhammad al-Naqid narrated to me: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us: Hammad ibn Salamah informed us, from Thabit, from Anas ibn Malik, that eighty men from Makkah came down from Mount Tan'im upon the Messenger of Allah, armed and seeking to catch the Prophet and his Companions unaware. He captured them without a fight and spared their lives. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: 'He is the One who withheld their hands from you and your hands from them in the valley of Makkah, after He had given you victory over them.' (Quran 48:24)

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us: Hammad ibn Salamah informed us, from Thabit, from Anas, that Umm Sulaym carried a dagger on the day of Hunayn. Abu Talhah saw her and said: Messenger of Allah, here is Umm Sulaym carrying a dagger. The Messenger of Allah asked her: What is this dagger? She said: I took it so that if any polytheist came near me, I would slit his belly with it. The Messenger of Allah began laughing. She said: Messenger of Allah, kill those freed men who came after us and fled from you. The Messenger of Allah said: Umm Sulaym, Allah has spared us and dealt well with us. Muhammad ibn Hatim also narrated this to me: Bahz narrated to us: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us: Ishaq ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Talhah informed us, from Anas ibn Malik, about the story of Umm Sulaym, from the Prophet, with a report like Thabit's hadith.

Yahya ibn Yahya informed us: Jafar ibn Sulayman informed us, from Thabit, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: When the Messenger of Allah went on an expedition, he would take Umm Sulaym and some women of the Ansar with him. They would give water to drink and treat the wounded.

Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi narrated to us: Abdullah ibn Amr (Abu Mamar al-Minqari) narrated to us: Abd al-Warith narrated to us: Abd al-Aziz (Ibn Suhayb) narrated to us, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: On the day of Uhud, some people fled from the Prophet, while Abu Talhah stood before the Prophet, shielding him with a small shield. Abu Talhah was a skilled archer who drew his bow powerfully, and that day he broke two or three bows. Whenever a man passed carrying a quiver of arrows, Abu Talhah would say: Scatter them for Abu Talhah. The Prophet of Allah would look out at the people, and Abu Talhah would say: Prophet of Allah, may my father and mother be sacrificed for you, do not look out, lest an arrow from the people strike you. My chest is before yours. I saw Aishah bint Abi Bakr and Umm Sulaym with their garments hitched up, so that I could see their ankle bracelets. They carried water skins on their backs, poured the water into the people's mouths, then returned, refilled them, and came back to pour water into the people's mouths. Abu Talhah's sword fell from his hand once or twice, or perhaps three times, because he was dozing.

Abdullah ibn Maslamah ibn Qanab narrated to us: Sulayman (Ibn Bilal) narrated to us, from Jafar ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Yazid ibn Hurmuz, that Najdah wrote to Ibn Abbas asking him about five matters. Ibn Abbas said: Were it not that I would be concealing knowledge, I would not have written to him. Najdah wrote: To proceed: Tell me, did the Messenger of Allah go on expeditions with women? Did he assign them a share? Did he kill children? When does an orphan cease to be an orphan? And to whom does the fifth belong? Ibn Abbas wrote back: You asked me whether the Messenger of Allah went on expeditions with women. He did take them; they treated the wounded and were given gifts from the spoils. He did not assign them a fixed share. The Messenger of Allah did not kill children, so do not kill children. You asked when an orphan ceases to be an orphan. By my life, a man may grow a beard yet remain weak in managing his own affairs and weak in giving from his property. When he takes for himself a proper share of what people take, orphanhood has ended for him. You asked me to whom the fifth belongs. We used to say it belonged to us, but our people refused to grant us that.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, both from Hatim ibn Ismail, from Jafar ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Yazid ibn Hurmuz, that Najdah wrote to Ibn Abbas asking him about some matters, with a report like Sulayman ibn Bilal's hadith. However, Hatim's hadith says: The Messenger of Allah did not kill children, so do not kill children unless you know what al-Khidr knew about the boy he killed. Ishaq added in his version from Hatim: 'and distinguish the believer, so that you kill the unbeliever and spare the believer.'

Ibn Abi Umar narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ismail ibn Umayyah, from Said al-Maqburi, from Yazid ibn Hurmuz, who said: Najdah ibn Amir al-Haruri wrote to Ibn Abbas asking him whether a slave and a woman who were present at the distribution of spoils received a share, about killing children, when an orphan ceases to be an orphan, and who are the near relatives. Ibn Abbas told me: Write back to him. Were it not that he might fall into folly, I would not write to him. Write: You asked me whether a woman and a slave who are present at the distribution of spoils receive anything. They receive nothing except a gift. You asked me about killing children. The Messenger of Allah did not kill them, so you must not kill them unless you know about them what the companion of Moses knew about the boy he killed. You asked when the name 'orphan' ceases to apply. It does not cease to apply until the person reaches maturity and sound judgment is recognized in him. You asked who the near relatives are. We claimed that we were they, but our people refused to accept that.

Abd al-Rahman ibn Bishr al-Abdi narrated this to us: Sufyan narrated to us: Ismail ibn Umayyah narrated to us, from Said ibn Abi Said, from Yazid ibn Hurmuz, who said: Najdah wrote to Ibn Abbas. He related the hadith in similar form. Abu Ishaq said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Bishr narrated this hadith to me in its entirety from Sufyan.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim informed us: Wahb ibn Jarir ibn Hazim informed us: My father narrated to me, saying: I heard Qays narrate from Yazid ibn Hurmuz. [Another chain:] Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me (the wording is his): Bahz narrated to us: Jarir ibn Hazim narrated to us: Qays ibn Sad narrated to me, from Yazid ibn Hurmuz, who said: Najdah ibn Amir wrote to Ibn Abbas. I was present when Ibn Abbas read his letter and when he wrote his reply. Ibn Abbas said: By Allah, were it not that I wanted to turn him away from something foul that he might fall into, I would not have written to him, nor would I honor him. He wrote: You asked about the share for near relatives mentioned by Allah, who they are. We used to think that we, the relatives of the Messenger of Allah, were meant, but our people refused to grant us that. You asked when an orphan's orphanhood ends. When he reaches the age of marriage, sound judgment is recognized in him, and his property is handed over to him, his orphanhood has ended. You asked whether the Messenger of Allah killed any children of the polytheists. He did not kill any of them, so you must not kill any of them unless you know about them what al-Khidr knew about the boy when he killed him. You asked whether a woman and a slave had a fixed share when they were present in battle. They had no fixed share, but they could be given a gift from the people's spoils.

Abu Kurayb narrated to me: Abu Usamah narrated to us: Za'idah narrated to us: Sulayman al-Amash narrated to us, from al-Mukhtar ibn Sayfi, from Yazid ibn Hurmuz, who said: Najdah wrote to Ibn Abbas. He mentioned part of the hadith but did not complete the story as fully as the narrators whose reports we have cited.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Abd al-Rahim ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Hisham, from Hafsah bint Sirin, from Umm Atiyyah al-Ansariyyah, who said: I went on seven expeditions with the Messenger of Allah. I stayed behind to look after their belongings, prepared food for them, treated the wounded, and cared for the sick.
Amr al-Naqid narrated to us: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us: Hisham ibn Hassan narrated to us, with a similar report through this chain.

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us: Rawh ibn Ubadah narrated to us: Zakariyya narrated to us: Abu al-Zubayr informed us that he heard Jabir ibn Abdullah say: I went on nineteen expeditions with the Messenger of Allah. Jabir said: I did not attend Badr or Uhud because my father prevented me. After Abdullah was killed on the day of Uhud, I never missed an expedition with the Messenger of Allah.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Zayd ibn al-Hubab narrated to us. [Another chain:] Said ibn Muhammad al-Jarmi narrated to us: Abu Tumaylah narrated to us. Both said: Husayn ibn Waqid narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Buraydah, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah went on nineteen expeditions and fought in eight of them. Abu Bakr did not say 'of them.' In his narration he said: Abdullah ibn Buraydah narrated to me.
Ahmad ibn Hanbal narrated to me: Mutamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Kahmas, from Ibn Buraydah, from his father, who said: He went on sixteen expeditions with the Messenger of Allah.

Muhammad ibn Abbad narrated to us: Hatim (Ibn Ismail) narrated to us, from Yazid (Ibn Abi Ubayd), who said: I heard Salamah say: I went on seven expeditions with the Messenger of Allah and took part in nine detachments he sent out. Abu Bakr led us on one occasion and Usamah ibn Zayd on another.
Qutaybah ibn Said narrated to us: Hatim narrated to us with this chain of transmission, except that he said both were seven expeditions.

Abu Amir Abdullah ibn Barrad al-Ashari and Muhammad ibn al-Ala al-Hamdani narrated to us; the wording is Abu Amir's. They said: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Burayd ibn Abi Burdah, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, who said: We went on an expedition with the Messenger of Allah. We were six men sharing one camel, taking turns riding it. Our feet became injured; my feet were injured and my toenails fell off. We wrapped rags around our feet, and the expedition was called Dhat al-Riqa because of the rags we bandaged around our feet. Abu Burdah said: Abu Musa narrated this hadith, then disliked having done so, as though he disliked disclosing something from his own deeds. Abu Usamah said: Someone other than Burayd added: Allah will reward him.

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Malik. [Another chain, with this wording:] Abu al-Tahir narrated this to me: Abdullah ibn Wahb narrated to me, from Malik ibn Anas, from al-Fudayl ibn Abi Abdullah, from Abdullah ibn Niyar al-Aslami, from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from Aishah, the Prophet's wife, who said: The Messenger of Allah set out toward Badr. When he was at Harrat al-Wabarah, a man known for courage and daring caught up with him. The Companions of the Messenger of Allah were pleased when they saw him. When he caught up with him, the man said to the Messenger of Allah: I have come to follow you and gain a share with you. The Messenger of Allah asked him: Do you believe in Allah and His Messenger? He said: No. He said: Then go back, for I will not seek help from a polytheist. She said: He continued until we reached the tree, where the man caught up with him and said the same as before. The Prophet answered as he had before: Go back, for I will not seek help from a polytheist. The man went back, then caught up with him at al-Bayda and said the same as before. The Prophet asked: Do you believe in Allah and His Messenger? He said: Yes. The Messenger of Allah said: Then come along.

Abdullah ibn Maslamah ibn Qanab and Qutaybah ibn Said narrated to us: al-Mughirah (meaning al-Hizami) narrated to us. [Another chain:] Zuhayr ibn Harb and Amr al-Naqid narrated to us: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us. Both report it from Abu al-Zinad, from al-Araj, from Abu Hurayrah, who said that the Messenger of Allah said (in Zuhayr's narration, attributing it to the Prophet): People follow Quraysh in this matter: their Muslims follow their Muslims, and their unbelievers follow their unbelievers. Amr said this was a report.

Muhammad ibn Rafi narrated to us: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Mamar narrated to us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: This is what Abu Hurayrah narrated to us from the Messenger of Allah. He mentioned several hadiths, including that the Messenger of Allah said: People follow Quraysh in this matter: their Muslims follow their Muslims, and their unbelievers follow their unbelievers.

Yahya ibn Habib al-Harithi narrated to me: Rawh narrated to us: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us: Abu al-Zubayr narrated to me that he heard Jabir ibn Abdullah say: The Prophet said: People follow Quraysh in good and evil.

Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Yunus narrated to us: Asim ibn Muhammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from his father, who said: Abdullah said: The Messenger of Allah said: This affair will remain among Quraysh as long as two people remain.

Qutaybah ibn Said narrated to us: Jarir narrated to us, from Husayn, from Jabir ibn Samurah, who said: I heard the Prophet say... [Another chain:] Rifaah ibn al-Haytham al-Wasiti narrated to us (the wording is his): Khalid (Ibn Abdullah al-Tahhan) narrated to us, from Husayn, from Jabir ibn Samurah, who said: I entered with my father to see the Prophet and heard him say: This affair will not end until twelve caliphs have passed among them. Then he said something I could not understand. I said to my father: What did he say? He replied: They are all from Quraysh.

Ibn Abi Umar narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, from Jabir ibn Samurah, who said: I heard the Prophet say: The people's affair will continue as long as twelve men rule them. Then the Prophet said something I could not understand, so I asked my father what the Messenger of Allah had said. He replied: They are all from Quraysh.

Qutaybah ibn Said narrated to us: Abu Awanah narrated to us, from Simak ibn Harb, from Jabir ibn Samurah, from the Prophet, with this hadith, but he did not mention: 'The people's affair will continue.'

Haddab ibn Khalid al-Azdi narrated to us: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Simak ibn Harb, who said: I heard Jabir ibn Samurah say: I heard the Messenger of Allah say: Islam will remain mighty until there are twelve caliphs. Then he said a word I did not understand, so I asked my father what he said. He replied: They are all from Quraysh.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Abu Muawiyah narrated to us, from Dawud, from al-Shabi, from Jabir ibn Samurah, who said: The Prophet said: This affair will remain mighty until there are twelve caliphs. Then he said something I did not understand, so I asked my father what he said. He replied: They are all from Quraysh.

Nasr ibn Ali al-Jahdami narrated to us: Yazid ibn Zuray narrated to us: Ibn Awn narrated to us. [Another chain, in this wording:] Ahmad ibn Uthman al-Nawfali narrated to us: Azhar narrated to us: Ibn Awn narrated to us, from al-Shabi, from Jabir ibn Samurah, who said: I went to the Messenger of Allah with my father and heard him say: This religion will remain mighty and strong until there are twelve caliphs. Then he said words that people made me unable to hear. I asked my father what he said. He replied: They are all from Quraysh.
